newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dassault-Aerospatiale merger would set new sectors.
newsitem.headline: Dassault-Aerospatiale merger would set new sectors.

text.p: A planned merger between Dassault Aviation and SNI Aerospatiale would lead to the creation of one or two new divisions in the new group and would not mean the loss of identity of existing units.

Aerospatiale chairman Yves Michot told the parliamentary defence committee the autonomy of the existing helicopter, civil aircraft, and space and defence arms of Aerospatiale would continue post merger, minutes of the meeting showed on Thursday.
"The merger will lead to the creation of one or two branches of new activities (business and combat jets)," he said.
The choice of how many divisions would be created was up to the Dassault executives, Michot said.

A privatisation of Aerospatiale should not take place before the merger, as this would delay the linkup with Dassault, he said. There are no particular partners singled out to take part in the privatisation, he added.
Dassault chairman Serge Dassault, who also addressed the committee, said the merger talks were taking place in "excellent conditions and in a positive climate," the minutes said.
Michot said understanding between the two groups had improved in the merger negotiations.
